en: Who is capable of understanding You [and] the way You stand [in all]
Becoming the five [properties] that pervade the earth [element]
becoming the four [properties] that abide in water
becoming the three [properties] that pervade fire
becoming the two [properties] in the eminent wind
becoming the one [property] that pervades the sky
[and] becoming the various different essences [in them]
gloss: participial noun, third person, noun, singular
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative

en: O Māyaṉ [born as] a cowherd
Having become the six [duties], the six [seasons], and the six [sacrifices]
having become the unique five [great offerings], the five [oblations]
and the five [fires]
having become the highly excellent two [qualities], and the three [states]
and the seven [qualities], and the six [qualities], and the eight [qualities]
having become various [types of] knowledge
having become the truth along with the untruth
having become the five [objects of sense]—including the sound—
along with the sense of touch
O primordial Lord who
—being [the master of] the five [elements], the five [organs of sensation]
and the five [organs of action] that exist in those that do not exist—
have become the five [subtle elements] and the three [producers of creation]
and the one [manas]!
Who is capable of perceiving You, who—being the five [immaterial forces]
the five [organs of sensation], and the five [organs of action]
staying put in the sky—are the five [senses of enjoyment] and five [classes]?
Being [the lord of] the thirty-three [consonants]
the five [plus] five [plus] one [vowels] along with the five [syllables]
being the three forms [of the three Vedas]
being [praised by the dvādaśākṣarī mantra with] three [plus] three
[plus] three, [plus] three [syllables], being the three [syllable-lit] light
being the undiminishing light, our supreme Lord!
What for did You accept [me] and enter my soul?
O Supreme Lord whom no one can fathom at any time
claiming that such is Your nature of uniting and mingling together [with the people]
Being the soul in each of the many bodies of static [and] moving [creatures]!
Are you not the primordial Lord who begot out of Your navel the four-faced [Brahmā]
in the past?
O You whose body is borne by a serpent!
The nature of protecting appropriately [and] bearing single[-handedly]
Mount Meru that bears heaven
the earth borne by the elephants/the snake Ananta
Heaven, the overflowing river held up by the sky
the clouds held by the great space, the unique fire, the five vital airs
is possible [only] to You
gloss: perfective aspect, third person, noun, singular

en: Taking one plus two forms, being sleep as well as wakefulness
being [the lord of] the three [periods of] time
being the earth [surrounded by] the ocean
being the three fires, O dark [Lord] who became a cowherd!
Can even the three-eyed [Śiva] praise You?
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, second person, singular
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: You are the god who is the original Creator of the celestials who are gods [who create]
[and] of the celestials who are gods on the other side, namely, the sky!
You have pronounced the end-time of the inhabitants of the sky who are primeval
O Time who are the origin! Who is capable of seeing You?
O [Lord] whose feet are worshipped according to the rules
by Śiva with red, thick matted locks
who [wears] garlands of laburnum pervaded by pollen!
O blemishless [Lord]! Rests in You the nature of being worshipped
by the [Brahmans] whose occupation [is to recite] the Vedas
with pervading excellence
[and] by those whose learning is based on sacrifices [full of Sāmavedic] chantings
gloss: pronominalised noun, noun, third person, masculine, vocative
perfective aspect, third person, noun, singular

en: Yours is the nature in which the static and the moving beings
get absorbed in You, being born and dying in You
Like the nature of the white, spacious ocean which rises, grows
and subsides within itself
with waves that rise and grow in it
gloss: participial noun, third person, noun, plural
participial noun, third person, noun, plural

en: You are the continuity of the [Vedic] words! You are the meaning expressed [by them]!
You are the light that appears unexpressed by [Vedic] words
Are people [like Brahmā]—born, being created by You, to create [the worlds]
with [the help of the Vedic] words—
[even] capable of succinctly speaking of Your qualities with words?
You create the world; You keep [it], squeezing [it] inside
[and] furthermore, You are born in th[is] world!
Ah! You do not belong in one place!
You remain distinct [even] as the world stays one with You!
Therefore, who in [this] world is capable of thinking of You who are deceitful?
There is nothing that allows [one] to say, ‘You are thus!’
Great people who have realized [people’s] disagreement [concerning] You
say that [You] are the Husband of the small-waisted Piṉṉai
Then, who is capable of thinking of You, with [Your] beautiful form
names, town, and the[ir] causes
unless they do [so] out of [Your own] affability!
O You who are pure consciousness! O You with a garland of tulasi shoots!
O Primordial God who slept in the deep ocean, becoming a tortoise!
Even though we are not capable of saying these are Your names
are You not the Discus-Holder sung about in the Sāma-veda?
gloss: participial noun, vocative, singular, second person
pronominalised noun, second person, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: Becoming the six [Vedic] components and the four Vedas
O You whose nature consists in being established in those!
O You with the excellence of abounding wealth
who recline on the bed that is the snake with red eyes at the top of the hoods
upon the wide ocean!
Are you not the Śārṅga-Holder with a body akin to the hue of the conch?
gloss: pronominalised noun, second person, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, second person, singular, vocative

en: Even if You come and stand so that the hosts of immovable [entities] see [You]
appearing with brilliance among the species [that belong] to top groups
[mere] particles, [or] mixed [births]
It is not possible to think [of You] through the meanings of words
of the vast, eternal collections of the Vedas [or through] ideas!
Your greatness is one that is reminiscent of the chains of mountains
O primordial God! You recline on the good ocean with the body of the snake
as [Your] bed
Furthermore, of what nature is Your being with a bodied form
Being with countless benevolent forms, one form, three forms, four forms
An enjoyable form, the [very] form of merits?
O ocean-hued [Lord]! What is this sleeping on the bedding
that is the serpent-bed spread out on the ocean water
[whose hoods] are a canopy above whose enjoyability never falls
Who has abundant light and gathered beauty
—[a serpent] that emits hot fire from a thousand poison[-filled] mouths
[and] two thousand eyes
Becoming a [haṃsa] bird, You uttered the four Vedas
Other than that, splitting the bird’s beak and hoisting the [bird] banner
You ride the bird, O you with a flashing discus!
Why, then, do you desire to lie down on the ocean
upon the true enemy of the bird?
You previously reclined on the ocean water spreading out a serpent
without any inhibitions
as the gods—who stand [for others] to praise [them]— came and sang [about You]
You lay down the other day in such a way that [people] insult [You saying]
‘O Keśava who became a tortoise that lovingly lives in the water!’
Tell [me about these] so that [I am] enlightened!
O Raṅga! That day, You churned [the ocean]
Wound the snake tightly around [the Mandarā mountain]
in such a way that the wavy sea was ruffled
in such a way that the trees surrounding the mountain wore away
in such a way that the great earth quaked
What did the gods who stood by do [then]?
O Father who rejoiced in [and] ruled over the apes!
Tell [me] about this in a special [way] so that [I am] enlightened!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative

en: O primordial Lord who, becoming an infant, slept on the banyan leaf
having thrust in and swallowed the seven worlds [protecting] then, now, and further!
O You with a garland of cool tulasi poked by bees!
O You whose chest is joined by the Damsel on the excellent lotus! O Lord of the Earth!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, singular, vocative

en: O You who, becoming a unique, white-hued lion
plunged the nails into the fleshy chest of [Hiraṇya] with bright, crooked teeth!
Are You not the Padmanābha who reclined on the milk-hued ocean
worshipped through yoga by those with the excellent four-fold Vedas of spreading fame
on [their] tongues worship?
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular
participial noun, second person, singular, vocative

en: O our great Lord with lotus feet that produced the waters of the Ganges!
O You who hold a discus, a conch, a staff, a bow, and a sword in [Your] palms!
O God of gods who became a lion! O You on whose chest abides
the Lady on the soft lotus that diffuses honey! O Dark [Lord] with an ocean[-like] body!
gloss: participial noun, second person, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative

en: O You who placed [Your] hands on and drove in the nails into
the chest of the bright-toothed foe, who had ample faith in [his] boons!
You begged [for the earth]. What is this deception? You concealed
the earth that [You] begged for inside [Your] stomach!
O Kṛṣṇa! Who can perceive Your intention?
gloss: participial noun, second person, singular, vocative

en: Becoming a woman, a man, neither, becoming the good one(s)
becoming the experience (of taste), the sound, and the sense of touch
O wonderful [Lord] who is not [the cause for just] one thing!
Turning into a cowherd tending cattle, becoming the truth along with untruth
O Thief who went concealing Yourself as a dwarf who nurtured the land!
gloss: participial noun, third person, neuter plural
pronominalised noun, second person, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular, vocative

en: O Flame that transcends the sky! O You whose form is shining knowledge!
O sin-removing Lord who abides in the land that is beyond [the reach of]
the Sound (=Vedas)!
Who can assess You [and] the way [You] measured the earth as a Dwarf
having gone begging [for it], with a countless [number] of tricks!
gloss: pronominalised noun, second person, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, second person, singular, vocative

en: O You with the greatness of digging out the earth [that You] created, measuring
Swallowing, and spitting it out
[and] of creating the watery ocean, blocking [it to build a bridge], lying upon it
and churning [it] previously!
O wonderful Lord whose broad arms with many weapons dispatch missiles
In such a way that Māli full [of anger] and animal[-like] [Su]māli enter Yama’s town!
gloss: pronominalised noun, second person, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative

en: Being higher than the highest, [You] rejoiced placing a woman on [Your] chest
having previously lain on the bed of ocean water; apart from that
You were born even among humankind. O Lord! O knowledge embodied!
Is anyone capable of saying that such is Your nature?
O lotus[-eyed Lord] who slept on the banyan leaf, having eaten
The sky, the earth, the mountains, and the seven oceans!
O You with good garlands of cool, fragrant, tulasi
with honey-containing flowers!
Are You not the [Lord] with the victorious arch that shot [earthen balls]
In such a way that [Mantharā’s] hunchback sank in?
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, second person, singular, vocative

en: O Death of Kālanemi! O You of innumerable glories!
O courteous [Lord] who became a unique child previously
having swallowed the seven worlds!
O warrior with a conquering anger that consists in bending the bow
So that the ocean burned!
O Lord who give liberation as per the intentions of the devotees
who are on Your side!
gloss: participial noun, third person, masculine, singular, dative

en: You are the Primary Cause who went upon the roaring sea
Taking along the army of troops of monkeys, and shot cruel arrows
so that the Rakshasas there were destroyed!
Are You not the Lord with lotus feet, which [You] placed extensively
And measured for Yourself [the earth]
Without the least compassion for the man who gave [You] land as begged [by You]!
gloss: participial noun, third person, masculine, singular, dative

en: O great [Lord] who shot a cruel arrow so that the Rakshasa
with lightning-hued teeth fell
blessed [his] younger brother, and gave [him] the kingdom!
O Husband of the simple Piṉṉai with a good complexion and sweet words!
Are you not the lotus[-eyed Lord] with enduring excellence and a golden hue?
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, dative
pronominalised noun, second person, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: You are the [material] cause, the [supporting] cause, the [instrumental] cause!
Because [You] are the cause of the [cosmic] egg, You are the untested flame!
That being the truth, You shine!
The wonder of becoming a cowherd, [despite] being the Vedas, the sacrifices
The earth along with the sky, and the Cause! What an [act of] wonder is [that]?
[You] were excellent becoming a fish that roams in water [and] a tortoise
[despite] being the Master with the discus; You excelled in affection
Besides, how is it [You] are our Lord, [despite] being the child of a cowherdess
with a fine waist that challenges a [young] twig?
gloss: participial noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect
participial noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect

en: Becoming the child of the cowherdess Yaśodā with breasts [adorned] with gold jewels
[You] kicked the cart, drinking the doubtful milk from the cruel breasts
placed [into Your mouth]
so that the sly demoness with a bird’s spirit perished
How [then] did [You] enjoy the nectar from the mouths of women
with gold[en bracelets] around [their] wrists?
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, noun, singular

en: Oh, they say, ‘Kṛṣṇa with hands that split open the horse
Causing the fruits of the tall, fruiting wood-apple to drop
And felling the flowering wild lime that opposed [Him]!’
O Vāmana, who—drinking the cowherdess’s milk, swallowing the earth
Eating butter, and drinking the demoness’s milk—
became a boar in the past!
O Lord who danced on the poisonous snake in a pond
Having broken the tusk of a mighty elephant with a rut flower!
O cloud-hued [Lord] who dance with pots!
O [Lord] whose chest appears with strings of cool tulasi garlands!
O Kālanemi’s death!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative

en: You picked up a hill and churned the ocean water
Other than that, You lifted up the hill and dammed up the ocean water
You destroyed Laṅkā surrounded by the ocean and encircled by ramparts made
Of hills. Aren’t You the cloud-hued [Lord] who lifted up the hill and protected
from the rains?
You protected an elephant. Other than that, becoming a cowherd boy
[You] killed an elephant; You grazed cattle, and ate cow’s ghee
And that day, You protected the cattle with a hill
And going on that day before the lady with kohled eyes with [red] streaks
You destroyed the bulls. What wonder is that?
Turning into a cowherd, You desired the bamboo[-like] shoulders of the cowherdess!
Who [among] the celestials and people of this world can search You?
O wonderful [Lord]! Is th[at] wonder an illusion? Apart from that
[despite] Your creation, You did the wonder [of ensuring that the creatures] died
Your wonder is wholly wonderful!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, honorific, sociative

en: O Lord who shamelessly went to destroy the bulls!
Speak of the reason [why You] filled with the red blood that flowed [from Your body]
the mighty skull placed in the hand of [Śiva] who put on the sliver of the moon
On the lowly locks, the distinct one who wears ash on the red body
who fit [the job of destruction]
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: O death who measured for Yourself the earth, having destroyed
The strong, angry Kaṃsa, after breaking the white tusks of the mightily angry elephants!
O You who extracted the life-breath of the demoness who had come with the milk out
of deceit!
Aren’t You the Primary Lord of the hue of collyrium?
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative
participial noun, second person, singular, vocative

en: What is th[is] nature that consist in [having this] world hide the [affable] nature of Māl
[the lord] of all four time [frames] filled with these, [namely]
the [white] nature of the milk, the [red] nature of red gold
the [green] nature akin to the outer green of the moss
the [blue] nature of the blue nelumbo in the pretty pond
[around] which bees open [their wings] and roam?
You are on the earth! You are in the sky! You will not be grasped
By the thoughts of those who think, being confused in [this] world!
What wonder is it that [that] You are [visible] to the eyes of Your people!
You are distant [to the others]! O our holy [Lord] who recline on Ananta!
O pure, beautiful [Lord] with garlands of tulasi from the uplands!
gloss: participial noun, second person, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative

en: O You with a head on which play garlands of cool, flowering tulasi!
Holding a horn and carrying a discus, You ride a winged bird!
Even if [I] do not have [even] a trifle of the goodness that the [people of]
the land have
do tell how I, a dog, will sever [the cycle of] births along with deaths
obtaining liberation!
gloss: pronominalised noun, second person, singular, vocative

en: O Kṛṣṇa with a cloud-like body! O Lord of the sky!
They say that You lie upon a serpent bed upon the water. Besides
They say that You do not belong to one place, that there are no limits
[as to where You live]. Therefore
Tell [me] how I, a dog, [can] learn about the place to reach and pay reverence!
Aren’t you the primary Lord who
—standing on the hill, sitting on the sky, reclining on the wide ocean
spreading over the unique world, on[ce] swallowing that, dug [it] out
as a boar previously—
created the good living beings during the days that went well
and protected [them] by establishing gods for them?
[Śrī]Raṅgam—with beautiful, cool water
where, as the heron moves away after eating the crab
[and] as the scabbardfish leaps
a barbus-fish roams about, securing the help of the blue nelumbo—
is the town of the Lord who rejoiced at heart
by properly dispatching an earthen ball
at the hump of the hunch-backed woman
around whose garlanded chignon bees wander
The town of the Warrior who, in the past, dispatched an arrow
with a robustly vigorous bow in hand in such a way that
the white-waved black ocean turned red and boiled away
is Raṅgam of enduring fame, which has groves with humming bees as [its] fences
[and] in whose pure water even the crowds from the eight quarters
bathe worshipfully
The Temple, which the four-headed Aja paid reverence to
which they call Raṅgam—with overflowing streams that become full, spread
cast gold [ashore], and wander back and forth—
is the lustrous place where the Lord—who bent [His] bow, shot arrows
cut off and caused the ten heads of the king of Laṅkā to drop—abides
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, oblique

en: Raṅgam with beautiful cool water, where those bearing the trident staff
[made of] mature bamboo with small teeth[-like nodes]
—who have set their minds solely [on Him and] have renounced attachment—
live considering [it highly]
is the town of the Mahout who moved towards and caught
the mature, forest-dwelling elephant, which came opposing [Him] in battle
and furthermore, broke [its] tusks
gloss: verbal noun, neuter singular, accusative, perfective aspect

en: Raṅgam with River [Kāverī] is the name of the great Temple of the primeval Māl
who cut off Bāṇa’s thousand arms
as the three-eyed [Śiva], who had obtained a shameful curse, along with Durgā
took the army that had come together with [his] people
and ran rushingly away from the battle
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: He who ruined Laṅkā by shooting an arrow [with] a leaf[-like] tip
is the Lord who dwells in Raṅgam by the Kāverī, which, being born in the mountain
comes descending, casts sandalwood trees [ashore]
and flows dashing [against the shores] with the paste emitted by the Kamela trees
that it had scattered, shaken, and broken
gloss: participial noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: Becoming the husband of the Lady-love who abides on the great lotus and Lady Earth
And besides uniting with the shoulders of Cowherdess Piṉṉai afterwards
O You who bestowed grace by placing Your feet in my thoughts
so that they last [forever]!
Aren’t You the [Lord] with lotus[-like eyes] who dwells in Raṅgam
surrounded by the Poṉṉi?
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: O Warrior who gained victory by going [to Laṅkā] on that day so that [Rāvaṇa] was
Afraid, and killed [him]
in such a way that the ten strong heads of the king of Laṅkā dropped on the ground!
Aren’t you the Māl who reclined in Kuṭantai so that [Brahmins] with threads
across [their chests]
—those with the Vedas on the [tip of their] tongues, those who had learned
The right [knowledge]—circumambulate [You]?
The ocean[-bodied Rāma]—who went [to Laṅkā], attacked and destroyed
[Rāvaṇa] who desired to stay on the breasts of the lady (Sītā) with braceleted hands
so that his limbs perished—
is the lotus[-eyed Lord] who reclined inside the cool Kuṭantai
with abundant water[bodies] in which women with long, fragrant locks bathe!
gloss: participial noun, third person, masculine, singular
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: O superior Lord who rejoiced walking so that the trees were destroyed
Attacking a rutting elephant, striking [its] head so that [its] strength was destroyed
And breaking one of [its] tusks!
O [Lord] whose feet measured the worlds, splitting [open] the horse’s muzzle!
Aren’t you the Māl who reclined in Kuṭantai
so that the brahmins obtained boons [from You]?
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: O Cowherd who joined the cool Kuṭantai with paddy fences, cool fields
Wide moats, flowering groves, [and] tall, pretty mansions!
O Warrior with a bow in hand who bent the bow so that the heads of
Kālanemi, [Dantā]vakra, Khara, [and] Mura united with Death!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, sociative
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: Standing in Vēṅkaṭam where the bamboos that had risen fall down
dry up, rise [again], and pierce the skies
as big dew [drops] that are pretty and fresh fall
aren’t You the Māl who reclines in Kuṭantai with fertile, flourishing, flowering groves
—where bees rise, sit, and remain—[and] pretty ponds?
Did the feet that walked hurt? Was the body—which scooped out
The trembling earth, becoming a Boar—shaken? Rise from [Your] reclining posture
in Kuṭantai—on the banks of the Kāveri with extensive channels
which cross big, obstructing mountains [and] difficult deserts—
and speak! May You prosper, O Keśava!
gloss: perfective aspect, neuter plural, third person
perfective aspect, neuter plural, third person

en: O worthy [Lord] from Kuṟuṅkuṭi where big, black palm fruits slip off and fall
into the pond in which coots play and the scabbard fish leap!
Is it You who are said to be the lion that rejoiced splitting into two slices
The angry, matchless chest of Hiraṇya[kaśipu] with bulging arms?
Entering and remaining in the thoughts of people who undertake the path of yoga
sitting properly
O Lord of gods who ended the[ir] evil karman!
Such affability as [You] stand and sit in the large Pāṭakam and Ūrakam
with hill[-like] mansions, and recline in Veḵkaṇai?
My Father standing in Ūrakam, my Father sitting in Pāṭakam
[His] reclining in Veḵkaṇai on that day was all before, when I did not exist!
I was not born then, I have not forgotten after being born:
[His] standing, sitting, and reclining are inside my heart!
The Wonderful [Lord], Anantaśāyin, the Primeval Being, Mādhava: [His]
Standing on a matchless hill, sitting in Heaven, and lying on a big, good ocean
Was all before, when I was not [there]
[Now His] standing, sitting, and lying down are inside my heart!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: Other than dying today and later, no one in the world
remains alive, [being] united [with life-breath]. Despite seeing that
how come the lowly people do not think of the flower[-like] feet
that measured the world the other day, go [up the path of light], reach
Heaven, and be a god [there]?
O you who will obtain the endless bliss of devotion forever
Going through the sun’s orb and obtaining liberation!
Drinking in with your ears and enjoying the purifying glories
of the lotus-footed [Lord]
Be saved, being liberated from the karman[-led] sorrow
that you are undergoing!
gloss: participial noun, honorific, second person, vocative
to drink in with the ears

en: The lowly people who join the two [guṇas] out of the threefold fruits
Become confused, being bewildered. There is no means of any kind
for [their] salvation
As [they] place [their karman] there, die, and go [into another womb]
If [you] desire salvation, live [by] praising the good Māl with cool tulsi
tied in a bunch
gloss: present tense, third person, noun, singular

en: O people who, thinking [them] as refuge, [seek] support and live by taking refuge
In gods without the power to give boons even when worshipped by
people with a bad appearance when looked at and by those whose reputation
is not sweet to the ears!
Are you able to sever your bondage of births worshipping our Cause?
The day [He] severed the thousand arms of Bāṇa who came [attacking]
In such a way that the gods connected [to him] spread out
And reached the celestial world
[with their] pikes, tridents, spears, large clubs, pestles, [and] swords
Only the immortals would know of their respective sorrow!
The day [He] severed the thousand arms of Bāṇa—who, furious
Due to the girl [like] a creeper swarmed by bees—came together [with the gods]
Our Wonderful [Lord] felt pity for Bāṇa, being embarrassed
seeing that the shaven-headed, ash[-besmeared Śiva], [his] sons, the god of fevers
Durgā, [and] the fire god ran away!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular
masculine singular, perfective aspect, third person

en: ‘The woman on the lotus, the Earth lady are [His] wives; besides
The four-faced [Brahmā] who dwells on a lotus is [His] son; to say [further]
His son is [Śiva] on whose [left] part a lady dwells, the bull-rider’
what the Vedic treatises thus state is the truth. On the other hand
If one speaks contrary [to this], it is not [the truth]
gloss: pronominalised noun, masculine singular, third person

en: Except for the people whom Our Lord, the Ruler of the celestials
—who shot on a previous day an arrow so that Vālin fell [and his] chest
was perforated, having shot an arrow so that the trees were perforated—
placed in [His] excellent thoughts
the full, permanent enjoyment is in no way for anyone, even if [they] rule over the sky!
gloss: participial noun, honorific, third person, dative

en: If one worships the two feet of Vāmana knowing [He is the means]
and knowing [He is the aim]
Wealth will abound, along with knowledge that grows in a dense way
If one praises Māl who dwells on the clear waves that rise up
It is natural that the grip of the evil karman that grows flowing out quickly should cease
gloss: imperfective aspect, third person, noun, singular

en: Performing good penance with a focused [mind] in each and all aeons
Becoming purified at heart thinking of His qualities progressively
Going further and further and becoming higher, higher, and higher
Which other god of gods can see our red-eyed Māl?
Except thanks to love that rises, with the heart ripening
—by [one’s] blocking the path of the lowly sense organs, sealing [it] with wax
opening the path of good discernment, lighting the lamp of knowledge
slighting the house of bones, with the heart melting—
who can see the [Lord] with the discus?
gloss: pronominalised noun, masculine singular, third person, accusative

en: Those who continuously prostrate with the eight different [limbs]
the primeval Lord—
who, being the eight [plus] eight [plus] eight [realities]
and the seven [islands], seven [mountains], and the seven [oceans]
is the eight [plus] three [plus] one [Ādityas] —
and recite the eight-syllabled [mantra]
will be capable of ruling over heaven!
Those who, with a [focused] manas—with attachment ceasing out of faultless love
[for Him]—
affectionately prostrate themselves at the good feet of the blemishless [Lord]
who lay on the serpent bed on the water
and recite his eight-syllabled name with love
will be capable of ruling over heaven!
Will liberation ripen for [people] other than those who are devoted
To the matchless Cause abounding in power, with [His] ten avatāras
[undertaken] for the good [to be] obtained by the [people from]
the fourteen worlds
Being the ten [directions] and the[ir] ten [guards], the seven [musical notes]
And the nine [rasas]?
gloss: participial noun, third person, honorific, dative

en: You threw Dhenuka—who came without love as a donkey and attacked [You]—
From [Your] uplifted shoulders, onto the good woodapple fruits
so that [he] is destroyed, with [his] days getting spent up
Who other than the people who desire the feet of
You, who [thus] annihilated [Dhenuka], can become immortal?
gloss: participial noun, third person, honorific, dative

en: Won’t you be saved by always seeking the feet of Māl, who
—reclining on the milk ocean that was churned, destroying Kālanemi
as Rāma, coming to help Vālin’s dispirited younger brother
discharging arrows [through] all seven trees that were closely set—
Reached Vēṅkaṭam?
O You with a glory that is higher and higher, by [Your] being consistent in any state!
For those who have given up ties, remaining with the thoughts strongly impressed
by [my] devotion for You
who slept on the serpent-bed upon the ocean with the three types of waters
All types of bliss will be possible here, there, and everywhere!
gloss: participial noun, third person, honorific, dative

en: O You with the garland of cool tulasi where honey spreads!
Even if [I] go up to heaven and reach indestructible enjoyment
By giving up [Your] golden feet
Will [it] be [like] the unparting bliss of love [derived from]
Tying up the manas with the rope that is eight and two (= pattu = bhakti)
gloss: pronominalised noun, second person, singular, vocative

en: Did [the Lord] with the discus make [me] be born again?
Or did He intend the day on which [He] will cause love for Him
to become firm [in me, with me] remaining at His feet?
How come our Lord has kept me, a dog devoid of love for Him or knowledge
in [His] mind?
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: O Lord who lay on the venomous serpent! I know that You are still truly capable
Of taking back and diverting [my] thoughts placed at [Your] lotus feet!
Therefore, saving [me] from your māyā
Do not confuse me with Your illusion, O wonderful Lord!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative

en: O You with the foot that kicked the cart! O Lord who danced
On the mighty hood of the snake that danced in the treacherous pond!
O You with a hand in which the conch thrives! If one meditates upon
[Your] red feet at all times, why do [You] not truly liberate [them]? O Kṛṣṇa!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: O You with feet which [Śiva] with a forehead eye, the lord of heaven (Indra)
[and] the lord on the flower [endowed] with good penance, along with other celestials
Worship according to the nature of [their] learning! O Lord! O [You of the] Veda!
To tell [the truth]
I have not had another attachment other than the attachment for You!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, third person, noun, singular

en: On the day the white ocean was churned so that it became muddy
setting up a mountain, stirring [it with] a white-fanged snake
[You] became a tortoise for the sake of the mountain [in] difficulty
and gave to the celestials the nectar that ends the[ir] pains
Would I value a god other than our generous Lord [who did that]?
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, honorific, dative

en: In order to end the excessive burden of the earth previously, [You] excelled at [driving]
Arjina’s chariot, performed wonders, steadily killed [the foes], gave heaven
To the mighty, victorious charioteers, and abounded in excellence, making the earth
[belong] to the five [Pāṇḍavas]
Would I value a god other than You [who are thus]?
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, honorific, dative

en: I was not born in any of the four castes
I have not learned the four good Vedas flourishing with goodness
I, a senseless person, have not conquered the five senses
O Pure [Lord]! I have not embraced anything other than
Your lustrous feet, O our Supreme Being!
gloss: participial noun, first person, singular, negative
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative
participial noun, first person, singular, negative

en: O You who crushed countless Rakshasas with fire[-like arrows]
For the sake of the Lady with a soft, melodious speech and large, weapon[-like] eyes!
I do not have any protection other than [yours], I do not have other close relatives
O [Lord] with innumerable wonders! Don’t ever remove Yourself from my heart!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, feminine, singular
participial noun, second person, singular, vocative
negative, participial noun, first person, singular
participial noun, negative, first person, singular
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative

en: O Cowherd [guarding] cows who, subduing the seven types of bulls
Embraced the fragrant shoulders of the lady with victorious, spear[-like] eyes!
Do say ‘Do not fear!’ to me who have sought refuge in You
who created the ocean water, blocked [it with a bridge], lay on it
and previously churned [it]!
O You who dwell in Raṅgam, show grace to me, who remain begging with desire for
[Your] feet that bloom, being pressed by cool tulasi pierced by bees!
O rock-candy made of sugarcane! O Kṛṣṇa who lies on the ocean!
O Rāma, archer who shot cruel arrows so that steel[-like Rakshasas] were pierced!
gloss: participial noun, first person, singular, dative

en: You are the life breath that dwells in the body! You are consciousness along with sleep!
You are all five [products] that abide in a cow! You are the purity found in them!
You are the earth along with the sky! You are the wealth in the abundant ocean!
You are me, too! Other than that, You are also our Lord, o Rāma!
gloss: pronoun, third person, plural, noun, locative

en: Taming the five sense organs that are hard to tame, severing attachment
to objects of desire, I came and stood steadfast in Your service
Thnking of giving up [me who did that], [You] did not act truthfully and
created excessive desire [for other things]
Despite [that], I do not have a protector other than You, who lay on the ocean
o superior [Lord]!
gloss: participial noun, third person, noun, plural
negative, participial noun, first person, singular

en: O You with boundless wonders! O wonderful Lord! O You whose glories are infinite
Even if [the people of] all seven worlds truly praise [You] for countless aeons!
O lotus[-eyed Lord]! Grant me properly the means to come and abide
At Your feet, severing the many, countless births!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, second person, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative

en: O [Lord] with excellent hands that hold a fierce discus, conch, staff, bow, and sword!
O You whose chest the Lady on the red lotus joins! O Lord!
You should bestow upon me the means to be saved, coming and reaching You
[after] severing the pain that is the body made of phlegm!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative

en: Without forgetting, [You] should bestow upon me the means for me, a dog—
whose desire for you has increased, renouncing anger, dispelling deceit
renouncing the desires of the five sense organs—to be released from the eddy
that is the great calamity of being born and dying, and further! O wonderful [Lord]!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative

en: [I] have heard that showing [me] the powerful sins I have committed
Establishing [my] manas in the [inevitability of their] fruits, [Yama’s messengers]
Are thinking of doing [to me] things that are not good
O Piṉṉai’s Husband! [Do] not [do that], do not remove me—who had tied my life breath
to You—from You, o bilberry-hued [Lord]!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative

en: O hard-to-obtain, wonderful [Lord]! You should grant me the boat that is bhakti
For Your feet, which is hard to obtain
Which is the means that lifts up to the banks [even] people with petty knowledge
who cause that which [ensures] leaving the eddy that is a great calamity, along with
births, to be beyond [one’s reach]
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, honorific, accusative

en: There is something that [I] say making a request: May You prosper, O Lord
whose nature is the joyful ocean’s!
If [You] have [it] in [Your] sacred mind to give an eternally superior boon
[then] You should intend [my] wandering thoughts to remain focused on Your lotus feet
And think [of them] uninterruptedly!
gloss: participial noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect

en: Tell me about a path that destroys the disease that is the body
for me who think about [Your] lustrous lotus feet out of unbreaking love
O wonderful [Lord] who lis on the roaring ocean! O victorious Warrior
Who became a boar! O King who made a path with hills across the leaping sea!
gloss: participial noun, first person, singular, genitive

en: O [Lord] whose chest Śrī joins and unites with! O Lord of the god of gods!
O blemishless [Lord] who are the law of the Vedas mixed with many hymns!
O Cowherd with a body [akin to] a pregnant, monsoon cloud!
Please tell the means of uttering Your names unceasingly and repeatedly!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative

en: O Wonderful Lord with broad arms with many weapons that dislodged and smashed
The heads of the harsh Kabandha, [Dantā]vakra, Khara, [and] Mura!
Do grant a continuous, uninterrupted chain [of thought]
of Your golden feet even when lying, sitting, standing, and walking about!
O You who are Time, who—swallowing and spitting out the earth, then begging for
and acquiring [it]
and measuring [it]—conquered [the worlds] thinking, ‘The earth will not exist unless
[it is] under [my] sight!’
O lotus-eyed [Lord] who rests upon the breasts of the lady with sweet words
that vanquish melodies!
There is no other form to contemplate other than Your form!
gloss: participial noun, second person, singular, vocative
participial noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative

en: O You who bear a discus, a conch, a staff, a bow, and a sword
That severed on that day [the head] of Kālanemi who became angry and attacked
In such a way that [he] joined Death!
Except for Your glory—of You who previously bore the hill on that day in order to
Destroy the evil that befell the herd of cows—
my heart does not have an[other] attachment!
gloss: participial noun, second person, singular, vocative

en: Other than for Your feet—that stole the days of the king of Kāśi with a burning rage
[Dantā]vakra, Pauṇḍra [Vāsudeva], the very angry Mālin, the great Sumālin, Kēśin
[and] Dhenuka
So that they were destroyed and fell—I shall not place [my] attachment and affection
Anywhere [else], our Lord!
Even if the lands—of Aja-Brahmā with excellent, evil-free boons
Hara-Śiva whose boon is [to cause] destruction
along with the land of the thousand-eyed [Indra]—approach [me]
Even when [I] sit in state having obtained the enjoyment that is liberation
Would I have in [my] inmost thought anything other than the desire to unite with [You]?
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: O You who shrank without there being anyone to compress [You]! O Great [Lord]
Who, despite shrinking, increased [in size] without anyone to cause [You] to grow!
As groups of ascetics with Vedic hymns in [their] mouths praise saying
‘The Lord of gods who ended the evil traits of self-conceited people’
I, too, praised [You]
gloss: participial noun, third person, honorific, accusative
participial noun, second person, singular, vocative
participial noun, third person, honorific, accusative
pronominalised noun, second person, singular, vocative

en: O dark Lord with cool tulasi around which bees wander!
Do forbear in Your inmost thought all this—the worshipping and praising of You
By me, a dog, being purified and without [being so]—
And show favour! O ocean-hued [Lord] who dwell in the thoughts
Of the devotees, as well as [on] the bedding on the ocean water!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: They say that it is possible for those who revile You [as much as] possible
by insulting You and for those who burned in the fire of Your anger
waging matchless wars, to come and reach You
Therefore, our wonderful [Lord]!
Take the offences that I, a dog, committed as [acts of] goodness
O Lord of the universe!
gloss: participial noun, third person, honorific, dative
participial noun, third person, honorific, dative
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative

en: As the days pass turning into swords, [our bodies] drooping [due to] illnesses
reaching old age
That day of death [has come]. Therefore, o my heart! Bow to and praise [Him]!
Besides, [with us] understanding well that goodness lies in being [His] servant
Māl’s feet should bestow [upon us] the enjoyment with no return
O heart! May you prosper! Think of
the excellence of Him who gave the fragrant water from [His] garlanded chest
To destroy the mighty distress of [Śiva with the] grievous sin—
he with red matted locks mixed with the waters [of the Ganges]
the black-throated one, who ate from the white skull
so that the sense organs were confused—
In such a way that [you] approach the good Māl!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular
participial noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: O heart! Worship and praise [Him] if you are capable of ruling over Heaven
Going above without suffering, having removed all eight inferior [issues]
Thinking of the feet of my Father, the Lord who, as a one-tusked boar, scooped out
The whole world, being knowledge, being the sun
Being the father, the mother, and our Lord who rules, the [Lord of] liberation
Mukunda entered and lived among us in order to accept us as [His] servants
destroying [our] many similar and dissimilar births
Why do you lie in the ocean of distress, o wretched heart!
Because the Warrior—who achieved victory by going to and killing
the sworded Rakshasa who opposed [Him], so that [his] days were wasted
turning Laṅkā into ashes on that day—
Did not set me inside Him as a separate [thing]
Can Yama part [me from Him] and count [my] past mistakes?
He who removes these—[namely,] fear, pain, distress, old age in the many births
the thoughts that [one] has, [and] the appointed bodies, in order to lift [us] to Heaven—
Acyuta, He with endless glory, He without a beginning or an end
the Lord who lay upon the bed that is a venomous snake
is the One sung about in the Vedas!
gloss: participial noun, third person, masculine, singular
participial noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: O Lord of the Lady on a fresh lotus flower! [My] heart—
[overwhelmed] in words, deeds, and a love that does not get severed—
has clung to [Your] flower[-like] feet
during the night with darkness and the morning with good light
Without dropping, being tied [to them] and has not returned!
O bilberry-hued [Lord] who dwell in Raṅgam surrounded by the Poṉṉi!
O wonderful [Lord]! Listen:
[Love for You], being kindled, arose in the powerful karman that is my soul
Came and dwelled on the bright, plump flowers called Your feet
getting entangled [in them] and remained everywhere without withering
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative

en: The liberating cloud-hued [Lord] [wished to] remove me from the many births
That do not leave
Came today and approached [me], mixed His permanent light in Him[self]
existing in me
Therefore, my soul severed all motions and obtained liberation that is bliss
which remains unsevered
gloss: perfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular
